references.text: The Amalekites are mentioned as enemies of Israel who attacked them in the wilderness, which explains why they posed a threat in the valley.
Moses recounts the command to turn back and head toward the wilderness in the direction of the Sea of Reeds.
The Amalekites and Canaanites living in the mountains struck down the Israelites when they tried to go up into the land in disobedience.
The context describing the presence of the Amalekites and Canaanites and their attack on Israel.
Israel set out from Mount Hor on the way toward the Sea of Reeds, fulfilling the command given in this verse.
The Sea of Reeds is mentioned as part of Israel's route through the wilderness.
The territory of the Amalekites is mentioned in connection with the promised land.
The spies' report that the Amalekites lived in the Negev region, while the Canaanites were by the sea and along the Jordan.
